close_reason: Fixed in 044b4f2: SpacePatchOp::AddMember now wraps a typed MemberCreate. All four Add* variants are uniformly Add*(<Create>). Cross-crate propagation to jmap-chat-server (5 sites) completed. Wire-byte-equivalent.
description:
What is awkward: SpacePatchOp (crate-jmap-chat-types/src/space_set.rs:257-302) has 12 variants with three distinct shapes:

  - tuple-wrapping the whole payload:  AddRole(SpaceRole), AddChannel(ChannelCreate), AddCategory(Category)
  - tuple-wrapping just an id:          RemoveRole(Id), RemoveMember(Id), RemoveChannel(Id), RemoveCategory(Id)
  - struct with id + patch:             UpdateRole { id, patch }, UpdateChannel { id, patch }, UpdateCategory { id, patch }
  - struct with two ids + auxiliary:    AddMember { user_id, role_ids }, UpdateMember { user_id, patch }

The AddMember outlier carries the role_ids inline rather than wrapping a 'MemberCreate' struct. The asymmetry has no spec basis I can find — addMembers in the spec just enumerates (user_id, role_ids), so a MemberCreate struct of those two fields would normalize the shape and let consumers pattern-match on AddMember(create) the same way they pattern-match AddRole(role) / AddChannel(create) / AddCategory(cat).

Why this matters even though it compiles:
- A consumer writing a unified visitor for SpacePatchOp (e.g. permission-checker, journal-replayer, federation-translator) has to special-case AddMember's two named fields against the tuple shape of the other three Add* variants. That special-casing is the kind of unprincipled drift that grows into copy-paste bugs.
- It is also asymmetric with the per-collection *Patch types: RolePatch / ChannelPatch / CategoryPatch all exist, but there is no MemberCreate counterpart — MemberPatch exists for update, but the create payload is inlined into the variant.

Suggested rewrite: introduce MemberCreate { user_id: Id, role_ids: Vec<Id> } in space_set.rs, change SpacePatchOp::AddMember to AddMember(MemberCreate). Then all four Add* variants are uniformly 'Add*(<Create>)' and all four Update* variants are uniformly 'Update* { id, patch: <Patch> }'. The wire format does not change — only the internal Rust shape.

Priority P3 because this is a Rust-API ergonomics issue that does not affect correctness, but it is the kind of decision that fossilizes once consumers depend on it. Worth fixing before the chat-server crate's handlers start matching on these variants in 5+ places.
title: SpacePatchOp variants mix tuple, single-field, and two-field struct shapes inconsistently
